citation: Paller, V.G.V., Labatos, B.V. Jr., Lontoc, B.M., Matalog, O.E. and Ocampo, P.P. (2011). Freshwater Fish Fauna in Watersheds of Mt. Makiling Forest Reserve, Laguna, Philippines. Philippine Journal of Science 140(2):195-206.

accessReview.method: Re-opened the official publisher PDF through its indexed web-text view. The PDF text was available, but a screenshot request for the table page returned HTTP 403. No access control was bypassed, no local copy was retained, and no source table content was transcribed into this review.
accessReview.textViewFinding: The official text view exposes the article abstract, methods and Table 1 text. It reports 12 taxa at Dampalit Falls, 12 at Molawin Creek and 9 at Cambantoc River, and describes sampled watersheds draining to Laguna de Bay. Those are historical source-reported counts, not a present-day inventory.
accessReview.fieldDateNote: The article gives a received date of 29 April 2010 and a December 2011 issue date, but the inspected text does not state fish collection dates. Neither publication nor submission date is treated as a sampling date.

reuseReview.finding: PJS describes itself as open access, while its Author's Guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form. No article-level Creative Commons or other reuse license was found in the inspected publisher information. Open access alone does not resolve permission to redistribute a structured species-by-site table.
reuseReview.nusCopyNote: The NUS-hosted copy is not being used for this text-view check. NUS terms separately require an item-level license or written permission for structured extraction from Digital Gems content.

decision.rationale: This refresh confirms a readable publisher text view but does not resolve table-image verification, current taxonomy, collection dates, waterbody crosswalks, or item-specific public reuse. Keep the 2011 survey as historical research context and do not turn its checklist into public app rows.

nextActions: Do not repeat direct PDF or screenshot attempts unless the publisher changes access behavior or provides a clearer official copy.
Continue with independently reusable museum or occurrence records and separately verify taxon identity, locality precision, date, and provider license.
If the 2011 table becomes necessary later, ask the publisher or rights holder for item-specific reuse terms before structured extraction.
nonClaims: The historical 12/12/9 site-richness figures do not establish present-day species richness or fish absence at any site.
No exact site coordinates, sampling stations, current water quality, fishing access, legal rule, catchability, natural diet or bait recommendation is established by this refresh.
